title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 51-53). Grothendieck is computing genus-0 Teichmüller-type fundamental groupoids for a configuration with maximal symmetry. Σ is the Riemann sphere with a real structure. The points R_i (i∈I, |I| = m = 2n) are the vertices of a regular m-gon, presumably on the equator. Σ* = Σ \ {R_i} is a sphere minus m points (a 'polygone régulier').

PΣ is a C*-type bundle over Σ, identified via (23) with V* = V \ {0}, where V is a space of sections Γ(Σ,L)(ω). Its restriction PΣ* = PΣ|Σ* ≅ V** = V \ ∪Δ_i. The Δ_i are the n 'diagonals', one for each antipodal pair of vertices.

The groups acting are:
- D, the dihedral group of order 2m, symmetries of the polygon;
- τ, the complex conjugation (antiholomorphic involution), with τσ = a the antipodal map;
- C*, acting by homotheties on V.

Page 52 is a programme statement. The goal is to describe, by generators and relations, groupoids equivalent to the fundamental groupoids Π1 PΣ* ≅ Π1 V** and Π1 Σ* (28). Base points ('sommets bien choisis') are to be chosen in these spaces so that the whole base-point set is stable under D and τ. The induced groupoid morphism Π1 V** → Π1 Σ* (29) must also be made explicit. This is the 'base points stable under the symmetry group' philosophy of the Teichmüller tower.

The full group acting on (28)-(29) is D × C* × {1,τ}. Marginal notes add two points: C* acts by homotheties (opposite to its action on PΣ*), and the action is not faithful because a certain element (-1) acts trivially.

Grothendieck then passes to the finite subgroup D × μ_m × {1,τ}, of order 2m·m·2 = 4m² = 16n² (144 for n = 3, the hexagon). It acts non-faithfully; the faithful quotient (D×μ_m)/±1 × {1,τ} (30) has order 8n² (72 for n = 3). He notes that one may also use the subgroup D^+ × μ_m ≅ μ_m(ω) × μ_m (31), where D^+ is the cyclic rotation subgroup.

Page 53 makes this concrete. The eigen-decomposition V_C = ⊕_{ω∈ω̲} V_C^ω (two characters) gives an action of μ_m^{ω̲} of order m². The kernel of D^+ × μ_m → μ_m^{ω̲} is {1, (a_0,-1)}, where a_0 is rotation by π. The image has index 2 and is cut out by (λ_ω λ_ω')^n = 1.
errors: No mathematical errors found on this page. The orders check: |D×μ_m×{1,τ}| = 2m·m·2 = 4m² = 16n², and quotienting by the order-2 kernel gives 2m² = 8n²; for n = 3 these are 144 and 72.
The element called '(-1)' that acts trivially is, per p. 53, really the pair (a_0, -1): rotation by π in D^+ together with -1 in μ_m. Writing it as '-1' alone is shorthand.
The page is only a plan: no generators or relations are actually given here.

ideas.what: Describe fundamental groupoids of a symmetric punctured sphere (regular m-gon) and of an associated C*-bundle by generators and relations, with base points stable under the dihedral group and complex conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with a Galois/symmetry-stable set of (tangential) base points; dihedral-symmetric presentations of π1(P^1 minus roots of unity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara; later Nakamura and Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §§2-3 (choice of base points stable under symmetries in the Teichmüller tower) and the Longue Marche manuscript (1981), in spirit

ideas.what: Comparison morphism Π1(C*-bundle over Σ*) → Π1(Σ*), i.e. the central-extension picture, with V** a complement of n lines.
ideas.modern_name: Central extension of punctured-sphere group by Z (hyperplane-arrangement complement; Hopf-type fibration)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Brieskorn, Deligne on arrangements; braid/mapping-class central extensions)

ideas.what: Symmetry group D × μ_m × {1,τ} of order 4m², its faithful quotient of order 8n², and the isomorphism D^+ × μ_m ≅ μ_m × μ_m.
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism-group bookkeeping for a dihedral-symmetric configuration with conjugation

missed.claim: The page announces explicit presentations of Π1 V** and Π1 Σ*, with symmetric base points and the morphism (29), for the regular-polygon configuration (n = 3 highlighted). This is part of a worked example in the Teichmüller-groupoid programme whose completed form is not visible here. A dihedral-plus-conjugation-equivariant presentation, including the C*-bundle level, is close to later work (e.g. Ihara and Deligne-Goncharov on P^1 minus μ_N), but this specific framing is not attributed to Grothendieck in the literature.
missed.quote: Je veux décrire des groupoïdes équivalents aux groupoïdes fondamentaux ... par générateurs et relations, avec des sommets bien choisis ... stables par l'action de D ainsi que de celle de τ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor historical point. It shows Grothendieck treating P^1 minus roots-of-unity configurations equivariantly under D × μ_m × ⟨τ⟩ around 1978+. That predates published work on cyclotomic/dihedral fundamental groupoids, though the mathematics itself is standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a programmatic statement plus routine group-order bookkeeping. Choosing symmetry-stable base points is a known Esquisse theme. The only mild interest is the early equivariant treatment of the regular-polygon (roots-of-unity) case with complex conjugation and the C*-bundle level.
transcription_corrections: The struck-out '($\mathbb{C}^*$, -1)' is more likely '($a_0$, -1)' or '($\mathfrak{a}$, -1)', the element acting trivially (cf. p. 53: kernel generated by $(a_0,-1)$).
The marginal note reads roughly 'NB action des groupes non fidèle, l'élément (-1) opère trivialement'. 'non' appears not to be struck out, consistent with the later 'opère non fidèlement'.
In the marginal note 'D opère topologiquement', the struck word may be 'holomorphiquement' or similar; the following clause is 'C* par homothéties (mais c'est l'action opposée de celle sur PΣ*)'.
In the left marginal note, read '(D×μ_m)/±1 × {1,τ}', numbered (30), 'qui opère fidèlement'.
'(144 si n=3)' is correct (4·36); the overwritten digits before it were corrections of the order formula.
